 RM13mil project to solve Kg Chempaka flood woes
 By GRACE CHEN 
 Wednesday, 11 Nov 2026

 bookmark

 Ongoing construction of a pump room at Jalan PJU 1/4A, part of flood mitigation works in Kampung Chempaka, Petaling Jaya. — Handout 
 Kampung Chempaka residents in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, could be spared recurring floods thanks to a Drainage and Irrigation Department (DID) mitigation project slated for completion by June next year.
 The project includes constructing a 2m-high retaining wall, riverbank protection, drainage outlets, pump gates and a Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) compact substation.
 It also entails upgrading a 1.3km stretch of Sungai Kayu Ara from Sri Maha Kaliama Temple at Jalan SS23/12 to Jalan Emas 1 in Taman Megah.
 Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) councillor John Leong said construction of the flood wall and access ramp near St Ignatius Catholic Church was ongoing.
 Teoh showing how she has to climb over the makeshift barricade in front of her door. The Kampung Chempaka resident says the work progress update has brought much relief. 
 “Work on the floodgate is underway and targeted for completion by late this month.
 “Meanwhile, construction of the pump house, control room, generator facilities and TNB substation continues at Jalan PJU1/4A, with the pump house scheduled for completion by the middle of next month.
 “Slope protection works beneath the transmission pylons parallel to Jalan PJU1/4D are pending a work permit from TNB,” he said during a briefing with residents on river upgrading works at the village community hall.
 The neighbourhood has suffered repeated flooding over the past few years.
 Leong said mechanical and electrical works, including pump installation, would begin once the relevant structural works were completed.
 “Efforts are being made to complete the project earlier, around April 2027, subject to construction progress, technical approvals and commissioning,” he said, adding that the entire project cost RM13mil.
 Additionally, Leong said DID tested flood-warning siren systems to strengthen early warnings for affected communities.
 During the briefing, he also told residents that MBPJ was carrying out additional drainage improvement works in surrounding areas.
 “A RM281,278 drainage upgrade at Jalan PJU1/4, Kampung Chempaka, is at 35% and scheduled for completion by February next year.
 “Drainage rehabilitation at SS25/4, SS25/10 and SS25/41 is being carried out under a RM349,962 project. It is currently 67% complete and scheduled to finish this month.
 “The combined contract value of these two ongoing MBPJ projects is RM631,240,” he said.
 Based on MBPJ’s flood mitigation planning report, Leong said several additional projects had been identified for future implementation.
 “In 2027, MBPJ proposes to construct floodgates and pump facilities at the Sungai Kayu Ara drainage outlet near the SS25/41 billboard, with an estimated budget of RM800,000.
 “A flood overflow control structure and pump facilities near Mayang Court Apartment in SS25/41 are also proposed for next year, with an estimated budget of RM800,000.
 “For 2028, further upgrades to the internal drainage systems in Kampung Chempaka, with an estimated allocation of RM1mil, have been proposed.
 “These proposed allocations remain subject to budget approval, technical requirements and implementation arrangements,” Leong added.
 Teoh Yen, 49, who has lived in the new village for over 20 years, said the work progress update brought great relief.
 “Residents have had to contend with floods up to three times a year.
 “I had to put up a makeshift barricade in front of my door to keep the water out, which means climbing in and out all the time.
 “I also have to change my mattress and furniture constantly (due to flooding); it is very taxing financially and emotionally,” she said.
 During the briefing, 20 residents including Teoh who suffered losses due to floods in April received financial assistance of RM250 each from the Damansara MP’s service centre.
 Present at the briefing were Kampung Chempaka village head Lim Yin Fah, and Alex Yap, personal assistant to Bandar Utama assemblyman Jamaliah Jamaluddin.
